text: Your data might be a little bit misleading.

text: And when I say categorizing, there are basically
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Very high level, but there are three things that you could find from those discussions.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: First, it's basically inputs about your model, so where your model is failing there.

text: As I said, I worked with several, several customers during this journey, and there are a couple learnings that I want to share that some might be obvious, but others it's very, very insightful.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the first one is the trust cliff that I like to call.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So what's the trust cliff?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So imagine you build a product, you are ready to ship, and you measure the reliability of this product, and you found 80% reliability.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: That seems fine, right?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Like, OK, I can give that to my customer, and they can start using it, right?

text: I cannot trust.

text: And why?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Because when you show 80% reliability, what they will think is, oh, OK, so if it's 80%, I still have to monitor this agent.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: If they fail, I will need to do some manual work.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So in fact, it's actually more work for me, not less work.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: I need to build this agent, plus monitor that, and also do some manual work after.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But when you get to a point around 92% reliability, the message changes to your customer and what they think is, okay, 92% I can actually trust this, right, to handle my tasks.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I completely hand over like a workflow to my customer.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So it's basically reliability is a zero to one, right?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Or you trust or you don't.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: There is nothing like in the middle there.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Second learning, it's the eval transparency.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So every time that you start working with a customer, you basically need to be transparent about three things that your product does.

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So what works?

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You can trust my product to just use my agent, and it will give you the reliability that you need.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Second point is these are the things that I'm doing to improve my product.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So there are some things that I know it's a gap, but I am investing time right now to make this better.

text: And the third thing, that's the tough one.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: If something doesn't work for your product, just go ahead and tell your customer.

text: Otherwise, there are so many tools in the market right now that if you show something for them that doesn't work, they will just forget about their product and they will move to the next.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So be transparent.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the main learning here is transparency on product limitation increase trust more than higher benchmarks.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: That's a very interesting finding, right?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Be transparent about what your product is capable of doing, and more important, what's not capable of.

text: That's how you earn customer trust.
